name: Capstone multi-architecture disassembly (cs_disasm)
description:
cs_disasm is the main batch-disassembly entry point of the Capstone library: given a raw byte buffer (fully untrusted, e.g. attacker-controlled binary/code) plus an architecture/mode handle created by cs_open, it walks the buffer instruction-by-instruction, invoking the per-architecture decoder (handle->disasm, e.g. X86_getInstruction, ARM_getInstruction, AArch64_getInstruction, etc.) and the matching printer, growing/realloc'ing an output cs_insn[] cache as it goes. This is exactly the code path exercised by every real-world consumer of Capstone (disassemblers, binary analysis tools) and is the most security-relevant surface of the project: malformed opcode bytes, truncated instructions, and architecture-specific bit-field decoding must not overflow the fixed-size cs_insn.bytes/mnemonic/op_str buffers or corrupt the growing insn cache. The core loop (in cs.c) dispatches through handle->disasm (arch-specific MC-style decoder), then handle->insn_id, handle->printer and fill_insn (which copies decoded bytes/mnemonic/operand string into the public cs_insn, handling X86 pseudo-opcode adjustment and user-mnemonic overrides), and on decode failure optionally invokes the SKIPDATA machinery (skipdata_size / skipdata_opstr / user skipdata callback) to resynchronize on garbage bytes.
- cs_disasm: target; drives the whole loop: initializes MCInst, calls handle->disasm per-arch decoder, handle->insn_id, handle->printer, fill_insn, and the SKIPDATA resync logic; manages the dynamically-growing cs_insn cache (cs_mem_calloc/realloc) and cs_detail allocation when CS_OPT_DETAIL is enabled.
- cs_open: lifecycle/source function that must run first; selects cs_arch and cs_mode (e.g. CS_ARCH_X86/ARM/AARCH64/MIPS/..., with CS_MODE_32/64/16/THUMB/ARM/MCLASS/V8/LITTLE_ENDIAN/BIG_ENDIAN/...), validates mode against each arch's arch_disallowed_mode_mask, and installs the arch-specific vtable (disasm/option/insn_id/printer) that cs_disasm dispatches through — this selects which decoder/core is fuzzed.
- cs_option: configuration entry; toggles CS_OPT_DETAIL (allocates/returns cs_detail structures filled by fill_insn/arch printers), CS_OPT_SKIPDATA and CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP (custom mnemonic/callback controlling the skipdata_bytes resync path in cs_disasm), CS_OPT_UNSIGNED (affects SStream_opt_unum formatting), CS_OPT_MNEMONIC (custom mnemonic substitution list consumed inside fill_insn), and per-arch options (ARM_option/X86_option/... through arch_configs) that change which sub-mode of the decoder runs — all of these change which branch of the core loop/decoder executes.
- cs_disasm_iter: variant of the target; the single-step counterpart that shares the exact same core decode/printer/fill_insn/skipdata logic as cs_disasm but lets the harness drive the buffer/address/size incrementally, exercising the same core with a different calling convention (no cache growth, caller-owned cs_insn).
- cs_free: consumer/lifecycle counterpart; frees the cs_insn array (and nested cs_detail) produced by cs_disasm, required to run the round-trip safely without leaking/corrupting memory the core allocated.
- cs_insn_group / cs_reg_read / cs_reg_write / cs_regs_access: consumers of the disassembled cs_insn's cs_detail, exercising the per-architecture group/implicit-register tables populated by the decoder/printer, i.e. more of the detail-mode data path that the core (fill_insn + arch printer) wrote into.
The input space a harness should vary: (1) the raw code buffer bytes/length (code_size) — the primary untrusted input decoded by the arch-specific state machine; (2) cs_arch (CS_ARCH_X86, CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_ARCH_AARCH64, CS_ARCH_MIPS, CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_ARCH_SPARC, CS_ARCH_SYSTEMZ, CS_ARCH_XCORE, CS_ARCH_M68K, CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X, CS_ARCH_M680X, CS_ARCH_EVM, CS_ARCH_WASM, CS_ARCH_MOS65XX, CS_ARCH_BPF, CS_ARCH_RISCV, CS_ARCH_SH, CS_ARCH_TRICORE, CS_ARCH_ALPHA, CS_ARCH_HPPA, CS_ARCH_LOONGARCH, CS_ARCH_ARC) — selects an entirely different decoder/printer core; (3) cs_mode flags per arch (CS_MODE_16/32/64, CS_MODE_ARM/THUMB/MCLASS/V8, CS_MODE_LITTLE_ENDIAN/BIG_ENDIAN, CS_MODE_MIPS*, CS_MODE_RISCV_C, etc.) which change alignment/skipdata size and decode table used; (4) count (0 = unlimited vs. a fixed cap) controlling loop termination and cache sizing; (5) address/offset, affecting relative-branch computation; (6) CS_OPT_DETAIL on/off, toggling the cs_detail allocation/free paths; (7) CS_OPT_SKIPDATA on/off plus CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP (custom mnemonic and/or callback returning variable skip length, including 0 or oversized values) controlling the resynchronization-on-bad-opcode path; (8) CS_OPT_UNSIGNED and CS_OPT_MNEMONIC toggling formatting/substitution branches inside fill_insn.
